newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended a static session slightly weaker on Wednesday, with no firm impetus driving the market and investors few and far between after recent interest-rate jitters, dealers said.
"It is a technical market at the moment," one trader said. "There's just no fundamental reason for it to go up or down right now."
Dutch bonds opened lower, continuing a late dip on Tuesday and drifted in fairly narrow ranges through the rest of the day.
"Buyers are really cautious. There are no end-investors at all so any action is between the pros," the trader added.

Brokers said the pattern of trade in the market was following a fairly set recent pattern, with buying interest in the long end, particularly the ten-year benchmark, and some offers in the mid-curve and shorter maturities.
While it was mainly uncertainty over a possible rise in U.S. interest rates that was braking the market, recent Dutch hikes were still putting some pressure on the short end, they said.
However, the guilder was firming slightly against the mark, which could take some of the strain off by removing the need for further rate rises, one trader said.
